text:
Mark Jankowski has 10 goals in 21 games for the Hurricanes, one fewer than he had all of last season and on a pace for a career year. He is 32, on his fifth NHL team, and fresh off a Stanley Cup with Carolina in 2026. Ten of his 12 points are goals, which tells you what kind of season this is.

It's a shooting season. Those 10 goals come on 6.3 expected, a 24% rate against 17% last year and a league norm of 13.5%. The chances are good ones, from dangerous ice, but our range for his true finishing tops out around 18%.

The rest is honest. Carolina takes 58.1% of the 5v5 shot attempts with him on, he kills penalties, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.14 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there last season (92nd percentile). They also noted his results trailed his chances in 2025-26, so this is partly a correction the other way. His ice time has slipped to 13.6 minutes over his last ten, with three goals in that span. Expect the goals to slow; the player is the same.
headline: Jankowski has ten goals and a finishing rate to match
